elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate for convenience
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement ... for convenience at the end of any calendar month"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days' written notice by Customer
elements.evidence: "providing at least 30 days' prior written notice to IBM"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "IBM will refund any Charges prepaid for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "IBM may not terminate this Agreement or any Service Option Attachment for convenience during any committed term."
notice set at "at least 30 days' prior written notice", below the 60–90 day fallback band

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A" — amount not stated in clause

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "IBM may not terminate ... for convenience during any committed term" (no end-of-term Vendor right granted)

reasons: All four preferred atomic elements are satisfied on the operative text: Customer convenience right, 30 days' notice, refund of prepaid Charges for the post-termination period, and an express bar on IBM convenience termination during a committed term.

The inserted phrase "without penalty" goes beyond what the preferred position requires (notice period, pro-rata refund, no Vendor convenience right) and was not needed to complete the level; it should be deleted.

"without penalty" directly contradicts retained subsection b, which still obliges Customer to pay "the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A", leaving an unresolved conflict about whether early termination charges survive.

Minor, note-only points: the retained "at the end of any calendar month" limits when the 30-day notice can take effect, and the refund is expressed as prepaid Charges for the post-termination period rather than the words "pro-rata" — acceptable in substance.
